Free independent guidance · A1–C2

Goethe and telc exam guidance from A1 to C2

Choose your level, then match the full examination name to your goal. These twelve guides explain the format, official preparation material and the next steps for a particular provider.

A1A2B1B2C1C2

Choose the certificate before the study plan

A CEFR label describes a level of language ability; it does not mean every examination at that level has the same tasks, scoring or recognition. Check the full certificate name requested by your receiving organisation before choosing a convenient date.

At A1 and A2, use the correct adult or youth version. At B1 and B2, distinguish general tests from dual-level or professional variants. At C1, general telc and C1 Hochschule require separate attention. At C2, telc includes integrated listening and writing while Goethe uses four modules.

Read the wider telc, Goethe and ÖSD comparison · Find official preparation resources

A1 exam guidance

Goethe A1 exam guide

Goethe-Zertifikat A1: Start Deutsch 1

This guide covers the adult Start Deutsch 1 examination. Fit in Deutsch 1 is the youth examination; a shared A1 label does not make the two task sets identical.

telc A1 exam guide

Start Deutsch 1 / telc Deutsch A1

This page covers the general adult Start Deutsch 1 / telc Deutsch A1 examination. A1 Junior and A1 for migrants are different named products. Begin by matching the full exam name to your booking and to the organisation requesting proof.

A2 exam guidance

Goethe A2 exam guide

Goethe-Zertifikat A2

Use the adult Goethe-Zertifikat A2 preparation set unless you have booked the youth version. Do not substitute a telc A2 or an A2–B1 dual-level test.

telc A2 exam guide

Start Deutsch 2 / telc Deutsch A2

This guide concerns Start Deutsch 2 / telc Deutsch A2 for general language. It is not the A2 Speaking-only product, A2 School, an A2–B1 dual-level examination or a vocational test. The full name matters when selecting material.

B1 exam guidance

Goethe B1 exam guide

Goethe-Zertifikat B1

This is the four-module Goethe-Zertifikat B1. The adult and youth versions share the level but use their own preparation material. Check the exact version on your booking.

telc B1 exam guide

Zertifikat Deutsch / telc Deutsch B1

This page covers the general Zertifikat Deutsch / telc Deutsch B1. DTZ, A2–B1, B1 School and vocational variants are different named tests. A shared B1 label does not make their task sets or result rules interchangeable.

B2 exam guidance

Goethe B2 exam guide

Goethe-Zertifikat B2

The Goethe-Zertifikat B2 uses four separately assessed modules. This guide concerns the general Goethe examination, not a telc professional-language or medical test.

telc B2 exam guide

telc Deutsch B2

This guide is for general telc Deutsch B2. B2+ Beruf, B1–B2 Pflege and medical examinations have their own formats and purposes. Check the precise certificate requested by an employer or other receiving organisation.

C1 exam guidance

Goethe C1 exam guide

Goethe-Zertifikat C1

This guide follows the modular Goethe-Zertifikat C1. Use material for the current format rather than an older non-modular coursebook. It is a different examination from telc C1 Hochschule.

telc C1 exam guide

telc Deutsch C1

This page focuses on general telc Deutsch C1. C1 Hochschule is a separate examination aimed at university contexts; C1 Beruf is another named product. Confirm the exact accepted certificate with the receiving institution instead of choosing by level alone.

C2 exam guidance

Goethe C2 exam guide

Goethe-Zertifikat C2: Großes Deutsches Sprachdiplom

The Goethe C2 GDS is a four-module examination with an individual speaking test. The optional literature-related writing route requires the current official reading-list instructions; it is not a requirement to choose literature.

telc C2 exam guide

telc Deutsch C2

This guide covers general telc Deutsch C2. It includes an integrated listening-and-writing subtest and is not a relabelled version of Goethe C2 GDS. Advanced preparation needs to follow this particular task structure.

Turn a guide into a preparation plan

Start with an official mock matching the exact examination. Separate missing language knowledge from misunderstood instructions and time-management errors. Practise a weak task in a new context, then rehearse the published sequence and use the correct assessment criteria.

The suggested preparation steps are Klarweg advice, not an official timetable or a promise of passing. Confirm fees, places, approved accommodations and resit conditions with the centre. These pages neither book an examination nor generate official scores.

Explore the existing 400 language practice lessons. They support language learning; use the provider’s official mock for examination-format rehearsal.
